##### Summary

::: {.card title="Summary" fill="false"}

AI infrastructure is concentrated, the buildout pipeline rises sharply after the generative-AI boom, and resource intensity varies substantially from site to site.

:::

##### Plot


```{python}
#| title: Owner Power
#| label: plot-owner-power
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.owner_power()
```

#### Hypothesis 1

::: {.card title="Claim" fill="false"}

**AI data center capacity and capital spending are concentrated among a small number of companies and projects.**

:::

##### Plots

```{python}
#| title: Site Concentration
#| label: plot-site-concentration
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.site_concentration()
```


```{python}
#| title: Power vs. Capital Cost
#| label: plot-power-vs-capital-cost
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.power_vs_capital_cost()
```

##### Result

::: {.card title="Result" fill="false"}

The concentration hypothesis is supported. Owner-level and site-level views both show that aggregate infrastructure estimates are driven by a relatively small set of hyperscaler and frontier-model buildouts.

:::

#### Hypothesis 2

::: {.card title="Claim" fill="false"}

**AI data center power and capital buildout accelerated after major generative AI milestones.**

:::

##### Plots

```{python}
#| title: Timeline with Milestones
#| label: plot-timeline-with-milestones
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.timeline_with_milestones()
```

```{python}
#| title: Annual Additions
#| label: plot-annual-additions
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.annual_additions()
```

```{python}
#| title: Capital Pipeline
#| label: plot-capital-pipeline
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.capital_pipeline()
```

##### Result

::: {.card title="Result" fill="false"}

The acceleration hypothesis is supported. Estimated year-end power rises from 435 MW in 2023 to about 17,280 MW in 2026 and over 39,000 MW by 2028 in the timeline snapshot.

:::

#### Hypothesis 3

::: {.card title="Claim" fill="false"}

**Data center resource intensity varies substantially by project and geography, suggesting some sites and regions may be more environmentally or operationally stressed than others.**

:::

##### Plots

```{python}
#| title: Power vs. Compute Density
#| label: plot-power-vs-compute-density
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.power_vs_compute_density()
```

```{python}

#| echo: false

```

```{python}
#| title: Continental Comparison
#| label: plot-continental-comparison
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.continental_comparison()
```


```{python}
#| title: US State Concentration
#| label: plot-us-state-concentration
#| echo: false
charts.datacenters.us_state_concentration()
```

##### Result

::: {.card title="Result" fill="false"}

The resource-intensity and geography hypothesis is supported. Current power is not enough to describe infrastructure impact: sites with similar power can have very different H100-equivalent density, and some high-power sites sit below the median compute-density level. The geographic views add another layer: estimated power is heavily concentrated in North America and unevenly distributed across U.S. states, which points toward regional electricity, permitting, water, and drought conditions as important follow-on context.

:::
